prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1331; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- Witnesses and the officer say the claimant was not in the vehicle when the crash happened.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: A rear-end collision was reported under the policy, and the driver is named on that policy. The claimant is represented by counsel, and a concussion is listed as the injury.

Entry 2: The damage to the rear of the vehicle is consistent with the impact described. Photos confirm some details of the scene, but no independent witnesses have been identified.

Entry 3: The claimant gave an account of the collision, and the same account was repeated in every conversation since. The reported concussion matches the kind and force of the crash described.

Entry 4: Medical history shows a small strain in the same area several years ago, which healed fully. Treatment has run somewhat longer than is usual for this type of injury.

Entry 5: A neighbor has said the car looked damaged some weeks before the claimed date of loss. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the repair history.

Entry 6: The responding officer and the witnesses who have spoken to us state that the claimant was not in the vehicle when the crash happened. This conflicts with the account given so far and needs to be reconciled before the file moves forward.

Entry 7: The file remains open pending review of the witness statements, the medical records, and the neighbor's information. Counsel will be asked to provide the claimant's whereabouts at the time of the collision and any further records.
